ai.literal: The wealth of compassion is the supreme wealth among all wealth; material wealth exists even with base people.
ai.translation: The wealth of compassion is the supreme wealth among all wealth, for material wealth can be found even among the basest of people.
ai.modern: அருளாகிய செல்வமே செல்வங்கள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் சிறந்த செல்வமாகும்; பொருளாகிய செல்வமோ இழிந்த குணமுடையவர்களிடத்திலும் இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts inner spiritual wealth with outer material wealth to establish the primacy of compassion. The poet argues that compassion (அருள்) is the greatest treasure one can possess. To prove this, he points out that material wealth (பொருட்செல்வம்) is common and can be acquired even by mean or ignoble individuals (பூரியார்). Because material riches do not require or reflect noble character, they are inferior to the wealth of a compassionate heart, which belongs only to the truly virtuous.

ai.literal: By the good path having sought, possess compassion; even if examined by many paths, that indeed is the support.
ai.translation: Seek the good path and cherish compassion; for, even if one examines various ways, that alone is the ultimate support.
ai.modern: நல்ல வழியை ஆராய்ந்து கண்டு பிடித்து அருளைக் கடைப்பிடிக்க வேண்டும்; பல வழிகளில் ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தாலும், அந்த அருளே நமக்குச் சிறந்த துணையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme importance of compassion as the ultimate virtue. The poet advises us to seek the right path of life and practice compassion actively. Even if we analyze and evaluate various philosophical, moral, or practical paths to find what is best, we will ultimately conclude that compassion is the only true and lasting support for human life. The word 'நல்லாற்றாள்' (by the good path) guides us to the starting point, while 'துணை' (support) highlights how compassion serves as our protector and companion.

words.gloss: to those who have a heart

ai.literal: To those who have a heart joined with compassion, there is no entering into the painful world joined with darkness.
ai.translation: For those whose hearts are filled with compassion, there is no entry into the sorrowful world of darkness.
ai.modern: அருள் நிறைந்த நெஞ்சத்தை உடையவர்களுக்கு, இருள் சூழ்ந்த துன்ப உலகத்தில் நுழைதல் என்பது இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the protective nature of compassion (அருள்). The author explains that those who possess a heart filled with grace and kindness will never have to experience the dark, painful world of misery. Here, 'darkness' (இருள்) represents ignorance and confusion, while the 'painful world' (இன்னா உலகம்) refers to a state of suffering. By cultivating compassion, a person is naturally shielded from entering these dark states of existence.

ai.literal: Enduring life protecting, to those who practice compassion, there is not, they say, one's own life fearing action.
ai.translation: They say that for those who protect all enduring life and practice compassion, there are no deeds or consequences that their own life need fear.
ai.modern: நிலைபெற்ற உயிர்களைக் காப்பாற்றி அருளை ஆள்பவர்களுக்கு, தன் உயிர் அஞ்சும்படியான துன்பம் தரும் வினைகள் இல்லை என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the protective power of compassion. The poet states that those who cherish and protect the enduring lives of other creatures (மன் உயிர்) and practice compassion (அருள்) will never experience terrifying consequences. The word 'வினை' here refers to harmful deeds or the painful karmic consequences that cause dread to one's own soul. The wise assert (என்ப) that such fear-inducing distress does not exist (இல்) for a compassionate person, as their benevolence acts as an ultimate shield.

ai.literal: Distress to those who possess grace there is not; the wind-blowing, abundant and great world is the witness.
ai.translation: There is no suffering for those who possess compassion; the vast, fertile world blown by the wind is the witness to this truth.
ai.modern: அருள் உடையவர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் இல்லை; காற்று வீசுகின்ற வளம் பொருந்திய பெரிய உலகமே இதற்குச் சாட்சியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet declares that those who live with compassion and grace will never experience distress. To prove this, the poet summons the entire vast, fertile earth sustained by the blowing wind as a witness. The phrase 'வளிவழங்கும் மல்லன்மா ஞாலம்' highlights the grandeur of the physical world, emphasizing that the natural order itself stands testimony to the peace and safety enjoyed by compassionate souls. By showing mercy to all living beings, one remains free from misery.

ai.literal: Wealth having lost, those who have forgotten themselves, they say, compassion having abandoned, evil deeds doing, those who conduct themselves.
ai.translation: Those who abandon compassion and live committing evil deeds are like those who have lost their wealth and fallen into mindless ruin, say the wise.
ai.modern: அருள் இல்லாமல் தீமைகளைச் செய்து வாழ்பவர்களை, செல்வத்தை இழந்து தம்மை மறந்தவர்கள் என்று அறிஞர்கள் கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the spiritual loss of compassion to the worldly loss of wealth. Those who live without compassion and commit harmful deeds are equated to people who have lost all their wealth and are living in a state of mindless negligence. The word 'பொச்சாந்தார்' highlights how a lack of grace makes one forgetful of virtue and human dignity. Thus, compassion is presented as the essential wealth that keeps a person mindful and righteous.

to those who do not have

ai.literal: To those without grace, that world is not, just as to those without wealth, this world is non-existent.
ai.translation: Just as this world does not exist for those who have no wealth, that other world does not exist for those who have no grace.
ai.modern: பொருள் இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு இந்த உலகம் இல்லாததாகிப் போவதைப் போல, அருள் இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு அந்த உலகம் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a clear analogy to emphasize the absolute necessity of grace or compassion for spiritual well-being. The poet compares 'this world' of material existence with 'that world' of spiritual or ultimate reality. Just as a person without material wealth cannot function or find happiness in this earthly life, a person devoid of compassion cannot find a place or happiness in the higher realm. The symmetry between 'this world' and 'that world' shows that compassion is as vital for the soul as wealth is for bodily existence.

ai.literal: Those who lack wealth will flourish at some time; those who lack grace are ruined, rising up again is rare.
ai.translation: Those who lack material wealth may flourish at some point; but those who lack grace are utterly ruined, and for them to rise up again is impossible.
ai.modern: பொருள் இல்லாதவர்கள் ஒரு காலத்தில் வளம் பெற்றுச் செழிக்கக்கூடும்; ஆனால் அருள் இல்லாதவர்கள் முற்றிலும் அழிந்தவர்கள் ஆவர், அவர்கள் மீண்டும் வாழ்வு பெறுவது அரிது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the loss of material wealth with the loss of compassion or grace. Those who are poor in material wealth can still hope to prosper and bloom at some point in the future through effort. In contrast, those who lack compassion are truly destitute and ruined. For them, to recover their humanity and rise up again is extremely difficult, as grace is the essential foundation of life.

ai.literal: Like one who lacks clarity seeing the ultimate truth, if examined, is the virtue performed by one who lacks compassion.
ai.translation: If one considers it, the virtuous deeds performed by a person devoid of compassion are like a man of confused mind attempting to perceive the ultimate truth.
ai.modern: ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தால், அருள் இல்லாதவன் செய்யும் அறச்செயலானது, மனத்தெளிவு இல்லாதவன் மெய்ப்பொருளைக் கண்டதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the virtue practiced by someone without compassion to a confused person trying to perceive the ultimate truth. Just as a person lacking mental clarity cannot truly comprehend or sustain the realization of ultimate reality, a person who lacks basic compassion cannot perform genuine, lasting acts of virtue. Compassion is the very foundation of virtue; without it, any outward act of charity or righteousness is hollow and unsustainable. Thus, the author emphasizes that compassion is the prerequisite for all true moral actions.

ai.literal: Before stronger people oneself let one think, when oneself against those weaker than oneself goes.
ai.translation: When a person goes to oppress those who are weaker than themselves, let them think of how they would stand helpless before those who are stronger than themselves.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் தன்னை விட மெலிந்தவர் மேல் துன்பம் செய்யச் செல்லும்போது, தன்னை விட வலியவர் முன்னால் தான் அஞ்சி நிற்கும் நிலையை நினைக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet teaches empathy and compassion by appealing to our own sense of vulnerability. When we are in a position of power, we often forget the pain of the weak and act ruthlessly. The poet advises that before we oppress someone weaker ('மெலியார்'), we should imagine ourselves standing helpless before someone stronger ('வலியார்') than us. This mental shift evokes the feeling of fear and vulnerability, which immediately curbs our desire to harm the weak, fostering compassion ('அருள்').
